name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP worker killed 9 Nov; power cut 8 Nov
summary: A Zaporizhzhia plant worker was killed by a drone on 9 Nov, a day after off-site power was lost; no safety-system damage
state: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power for about 10 hours on 8 Nov and ran on diesel generators; IAEA Director General Grossi called it the 27th such event of the conflict (Kyiv Independent). On 9 Nov a plant worker was killed in a drone strike, the second since late October, and the IAEA said such attacks violate nuclear safety pillars (The Moscow Times). Searches on 17 Nov found no damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release.
for_you: No radiological release has been reported. People in the region should follow guidance from national authorities and the IAEA.
rubric_hit: Watch: loss of all off-site power (8 Nov) and attacks near the plant; no safety-system damage or INES 2+ for Alert

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
